public_final_quotes: Reviewed all four reply units against the complete current prefix and all supplied past sessions. The empathy and framing in R001-R002 match C:T006 and C:T008. R003's only checkable personal reference is supported, while its manager/coping suggestions are advice and exploratory questions. R004 is an open choice question. The mention of team morale/productivity is treated as a suggested discussion topic rather than an asserted user history; no user-specific factual or boundary error is apparent.

The reply accurately reflects the user's reported frustration about favoritism and injustice, normalizes it, and offers two practical directions—raise it with the manager or focus on coping—while asking which the user prefers. That is responsive and appropriate for this early, exploratory point; no identity or boundary issue is present.
The user reported that the peers' favoritism bothers them and that they cannot tolerate injustice, directly supporting the reflection about frustration and unfair treatment.
The user said peers hardly work yet are favored because they always agree with the manager, so the reply's description of favoritism not aligning with work ethic is grounded in the report.
The back-reference 'you mentioned you can't tolerate injustice' is directly supported by C:T008; the manager conversation is offered as a question/option, not asserted as a known personal fact.
This is an open question about whether the user wants coping strategies without involving others; it makes no checkable personal factual assertion.
